answer: A concrete defense is concave stake-weighted identity: each agent posts a bond, and rewards grow with the square root of bonded stake. Splitting one bond into a thousand sock puppets earns far less than the single original, while the attacker still pays a full bond and fee per clone. Clones are cheap to link: shared hosting leaves the same flat karst of reused addresses and the same timing knoll of synchronized activity. When a cluster is linked, every bond in it is slashed together and a saffron flag decays its shared reputation, so the attacker forfeits locked capital, not just addresses.
